_comment: Syllabus facts, extracted from Rameen's own class notes in source-notes/. Used in two places: the owl's speech bubble when a student clicks it, and the student dashboard's fact-of-the-day banner (which rotates one subject per day). Each item has 'subject' (history | geography | islamiyat), 'tag' (fact, tip, or date) and the 'text' shown. How to edit: see data/README.md.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The War of Independence broke out at Meerut in May 1857.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The spark was the greased cartridge: soldiers were punished for refusing to bite cartridges greased with cow and pig fat.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The greased cartridges offended both faiths — the cow is sacred to Hindus, the pig forbidden in Islam.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: From Meerut the revolt spread to Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi and Bihar, turning a local mutiny into a wider uprising.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal emperor, was declared symbolic leader of the revolt in Delhi.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Rani Lakshmi Bai of Jhansi led the fight against the British herself rather than surrender her kingdom.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Nana Sahib led the revolt in Kanpur; Kunwar Singh led the resistance in Bihar.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Farmers, villagers and women supported the 1857 revolt too — it was never only a military mutiny.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Under the Doctrine of Lapse the British could confiscate the land of any ruler without a natural male heir.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: English replaced Persian as the official language of administration in 1834.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The British moved Bahadur Shah II out of Delhi's Red Fort to the far poorer Qutub Sahib.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Banning suttee and introducing co-education were both seen as British interference in religion.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Indian troops sent to fight in Afghanistan angered Hindu soldiers, who did not want to leave Mother India, and Muslim soldiers, who did not want to fight fellow Muslims.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Rumours that soldiers would be forced to convert to Christianity fuelled the revolt in the army.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Most sepoys were Indian while officer posts were almost all British — a standing grievance in the army.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Nana Sahib only wanted the Doctrine of Lapse reversed — the rebels had no common purpose, which weakened them.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Hindus and Sikhs saw the war as an attempt to restore Mughal rule, so they withheld their support.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The ruler of Kashmir sent 2,000 troops to help the British — princely support weakened the rebels further.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Lord Canning's conciliatory policy promised that rebels who gave up their arms would not be punished.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Bahadur Shah II was aged and more interested in poetry than combat — his weak leadership contributed to the failure.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Thanks to the Industrial Revolution the British had modern weapons, while the Indians fought with outdated ones.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: In a 'more important than' essay, compare the two sides directly — don't just write two separate lists.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Political and social reasons explain long-term resentment; military reasons explain the spark that lit 1857.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: A 'was it the ONLY reason?' question needs both sides — points that agree and points that disagree.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: Bahadur Shah II appears twice: as a symbol of resentment, and as an incompetent leader. Two different arguments — don't mix them.

facts.subject: history
facts.text: The greased cartridges are the most commonly quoted trigger in this topic — know the detail, including why both faiths were offended.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: 97% of the world's water is salty and only 3% is fresh — and of that 3%, about 70% is locked up as snow.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: The Indus is Pakistan's main river system. Its eastern tributaries are the Sutlej, Jhelum, Ravi and Chenab.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: The Indus' western tributaries include the Swat, Kabul, Gomal, Kurram, Tochi and Zhob.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: River discharge is measured in cusecs (cubic feet per second) or cumecs (cubic metres per second).

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: The Indus discharge peaks in June and July — Karakoram and Hindu Kush glaciers melt, and the monsoon arrives.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Balochistan's rivers are small, seasonal and inland, so they are not suitable for irrigation, barrages or HEP.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Quetta matters most in Balochistan's drainage because its height brings more snowfall and winter depressions.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: The Indus Water Treaty was signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan, with help from the UN.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Under the Indus Water Treaty Pakistan got the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab; India got the Beas, Sutlej and Ravi.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: The Indus Water Treaty covered Tarbela and Mangla dams, five barrages and eight link canals.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: India cut off water supplies in 1948, causing failed crops and famine — this is why the Indus Water Treaty was needed.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Large dams: Mangla on the Jhelum, Tarbela on the Indus, Warsak on the Kabul, Kurramgarhi on the Tochi.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Warsak Dam irrigates about 48,000 hectares while the small Rawal Dam irrigates only about 5,000.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Barrages are longer than dams, dams are higher — and barrages produce no electricity because they sit on flat land.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Pakistan's barrages include Guddu, Taunsa, Jinnah, Kotri and Rasul.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Link canals move water from the western rivers to the eastern ones, to make up for water lost to India.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Traditional irrigation: charsa, Persian wheel, karez and inundation canals. Modern: perennial canals, tube wells and sprinklers.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: A karez is an underground horizontal canal used in Balochistan — being underground, it loses far less water to evaporation.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Inundation canals (barsati naale) only carry water in the rainy season, so they are unreliable — but they don't cause waterlogging.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Waterlogging happens when too much irrigation raises the water table; evaporation then leaves salt that poisons the crops.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Waterlogging and salinity are tackled with gypsum, lined canals, tube wells, surface drains and eucalyptus trees.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Siltation is the deposition of rock, sand and silt in rivers and dams — caused by deforestation and unlined canals.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Coal quality runs Anthracite, Bituminous, Lignite, Peat — and anthracite, the best, is not found in Pakistan.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Pakistan's coalfields: Quetta (Degari, Sharig, Mach, Harnai), Lower Sindh (Lakhra, Jhimpir, Sonda), Makerwal and the Salt Range.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Coal is mined by shaft mining when it's deep, adit mining when it's in a hillside, and open cast when it outcrops on the surface.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Oil collects in an anticline between two non-porous rocks, with gas above it and water below — an oil trap.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Pakistan's oilfields sit on the Potwar Plateau (Meyal, Balkassar, Dhullian, Tut) and in Lower Sindh.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Pakistan's refineries are at Karachi, Mahmood Kot near Multan, and Morgah in Rawalpindi.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Transport takes about 42% of Pakistan's oil and power stations about 38% — farming takes only around 2%.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Sui in Balochistan is Pakistan's main gas field — gas is cheap because it's produced at home, not imported.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Fossil fuels supply about 64% of Pakistan's energy, hydel about 27%, and nuclear plus other renewables about 9%.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: A good dam site needs a deep narrow valley with steep sides, impervious rock beneath, and glaciers or high rainfall above.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Best sites in Pakistan: solar in the deserts, wind on the coast and mountains, HEP in mountain valleys, wave energy along the coast.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Load shedding simply means planned power cuts.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Electricity is short because machinery is old, silt cuts reservoir capacity, winter rainfall is low, and demand keeps rising.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Pakistan aims to generate 60% of its power from renewables by 2030 — yet coal stations went from one in 2016 to nine by 2019.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Paper 2 is 50% of your O Level: 90 minutes, 75 marks, and you answer only three questions out of five.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: In part (d), a one-sided answer caps your marks however much you write — argue both sides and finish with a judgement.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: 'Compare' means similarities AND differences — two separate descriptions are not a comparison.

facts.subject: geography
facts.text: Name real Pakistani places — Tarbela, Sui, Guddu, Thar — rather than writing in general terms.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and became obligatory in the 2nd year of Hijrah.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat is mentioned 32 times in the Qur'an, very often right alongside Salah.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat is paid at 2.5% of qualifying wealth — but only once it has been held for a complete lunar year.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The Nisab for gold is 7.5 tolas and for silver 52.5 tolas.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Not everything is at 2.5%: mines are charged 20%, and agricultural produce 10% if rain-fed or 5% if irrigated.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Surah At-Taubah 9:60 names all eight recipients of Zakat — giving it outside those categories is not valid.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The eight recipients are the Fuqara, Masakeen, Amileen, Mu'allafatul-Quloob, Fi-Riqab, Gharimeen, Fee Sabeelillah and Ibn-As-Sabeel.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat cannot be given to a wife, children or parents — supporting them is already a Muslim's duty (Nafaqah).

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The Banu Hashim, the Prophet's (pbuh) descendants, do not receive Zakat, as a matter of honour.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat ul-Fitr is a separate, smaller charity given at the end of Ramadan so the poor can also celebrate Eid.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: In Pakistan the government deducts Zakat from bank savings on the 1st of Ramadan and distributes it through Zakat Committees.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The word Zakat itself means purification — it cleanses the wealth that remains.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Surah At-Taubah 9:34-35 warns of a painful punishment for those who hoard gold and silver instead of spending it.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) took up arms against those who refused to pay Zakat after the Prophet's (pbuh) death.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Belief in angels is the second Article of Faith — without it, a Muslim's Iman is incomplete.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Angels are created from light, humans from clay and Jinn from fire.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Angels are genderless and have no free will, so they are not accountable on the Day of Judgement.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The Qur'an describes angels with wings 'two, three and four'; a Hadith says Jibrael (AS) had 600.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Jibrael (AS) is the chief of the angels — he brought revelation to every Prophet and led the Night of Mi'raj.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Israfil (AS) will blow the trumpet twice: once to end all life, once to raise the dead.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Izrael (AS) is the Angel of Death; Mikael (AS) is responsible for rain, food and the celestial bodies.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The Kiram-un-Katibeen record every deed — one angel on the right for good, one on the left for bad.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Munkir and Nakir question the dead in the grave about their faith, their Lord and their Prophet.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Malik is the keeper of Hellfire and Rizwan the keeper of Paradise.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: At Badr, the Qur'an says Allah answered the believers: 'I will assist you with a thousand angels, ranks on ranks.'

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: The angels prostrated before Hazrat Adam (AS) — showing that humans hold a higher rank as Allah's Khalifah on earth.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: In a 10-mark Zakat question, name all eight recipients with their Arabic terms — listing only four or five loses marks.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Zakat is obligatory (Fard); Sadaqah is voluntary. Don't use the two words interchangeably.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Iblis was from the Jinn, not an angel — angels cannot disobey Allah, which is exactly why this matters.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Kiram-un-Katibeen record deeds during life; Munkir and Nakir question after death. Easy pair to mix up.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Listing features without explaining why the belief matters caps a 10-mark answer at Level 3 — always cover significance.

facts.subject: islamiyat
facts.text: Part (a) is what Muslims believe; part (b) is why it matters today. Don't repeat (a) in (b).
